ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, legal representatives, and authorized incorporators against the OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, Colombian UIAF PEP database, Superintendencia de Sociedades corporate-disqualification registry, and Procuraduría General disciplinary records; enhanced due diligence and beneficial-ownership escalation required on any positive or ambiguous match.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá – Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) online portal (www.rue.com.co / www.ccb.org.co)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be composed in Spanish or accepted Latin-script transliteration using standard Roman characters; the name must end with the suffix 'S.A.S.'; pseudo-foreign, non-Latin, or graphically misleading names are rejected by the Chamber of Commerce.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The reservation is valid for 30 calendar days after issuance by the local Chamber of Commerce and cannot be administratively extended; upon expiry, a new homonym search and reservation must be initiated. If the name is rejected, the incorporator may file a 'recurso de reposición' directly with the issuing Chamber within 10 business days, and a subsidiary 'recurso de apelación' before the Superintendencia de Sociedades within the same procedural deadline; alternatively, a new name may be submitted immediately through the RUES portal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for an S.A.S. as the registered address, provided a Colombian service provider maintains the physical mailbox, receives official communications, and the company demonstrates an operational business capacity when requested; a pure virtual-only address raises commercial-substance risk for low-risk PR operations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 15% for a low-risk public-relations agency with a foreign UBO; approximately 30% if the registered office is virtual and no physical local personnel can be evidenced.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 1258 of 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada); Colombian Commercial Code (Decree 410 of 1971) Articles 98, 110, 373; Regulatory Decree 1074 of 2015
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Camara de Comercio de Bogota (or other Colombian Chamber of Commerce with territorial jurisdiction) - Registro Mercantil; Superintendencia de Sociedades for post-incorporation oversight
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitucion (private incorporation document) filed with the Chamber of Commerce; notarized public deed required only if real estate or assets requiring public registration are contributed
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum paid-up capital for an S.A.S. under Law 1258 of 2008; capital is freely subscribed and may be paid in installments over a term not exceeding two years as stated in the by-laws; no escrow account or formal capital deposit account is required at incorporation stage, provided the payment schedule and default remedies are recorded in the by-laws
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: IN THE CITY OF BOGOTA, D.C., the founding shareholders of [COMPANY NAME] S.A.S. convened and unanimously adopted this First Board Resolution: 1. The share subscriptions and the capital payment schedule set out in the incorporation instrument are ratified and accepted. 2. The registered office is fixed at the address indicated in the by-laws in Bogota, Colombia; the Legal Representative may open branches or relocate the registered office with due administrative authorization. 3. [FULL NAME] is appointed Legal Representative with full powers under the by-laws, and the entity is authorized to comply with governance, tax, and reporting obligations. 4. The Legal Representative is authorized to execute filings, open bank accounts, and sign management contracts. 5. All by-laws, corporate books, and internal policies are ratified. Approved unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability Search and Reservation (Certificado de Homonimia)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Camara de Comercio de Bogota - Registro Mercantil (online portal / service window)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name-search request through the Chamber of Commerce electronic form or in-person window, indicating the proposed corporate name and, if requested, a secondary alternate name; the registry checks for identical or confusingly similar names in the merchant register; upon approval, obtain the certification that reserves the name for a validity period of 30 calendar days.
required_dossiers: Request form for name availability
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity, promptly file a new request with a materially distinct corporate name; a request may also be escalated to the Chamber's legal division for a formal justification of the rejection or for confirmation of the right to use the name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Incorporation Instrument and By-Laws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Parties/Founding Shareholders; Notary 1 of the respective Notary Circle (only for notarization of the private document when real property is contributed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Documento Privado de Constitucion in Spanish containing: corporate name, registered office, corporate purpose (international media relations and public relations services under ISIC 7310), capital terms, number and classes of shares, board structure, representation powers, and by-laws; all founding shareholders or their authorized representatives must sign; if real estate is contributed, the document must be executed by public deed before a notary and registered at the Registry of Public Instruments Office.
required_dossiers: Name availability certificate (previous step)
Draft incorporation document and by-laws
Valid identification documents or passports of all founding shareholders
Power of attorney if execution is via an authorized representative
Lease or title evidence of the registered office address (for by-law identification)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber of Commerce rejects the document for substantive defects, prepare a corrective addendum ratified by all shareholders or issue a rectified private document and file it anew; any missing notarization, if real property is involved, must be completed before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Merchant Registration and Company Filing before the Chamber of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Camara de Comercio with territorial jurisdiction (e.g., Camara de Comercio de Bogota)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed private incorporation document and the mandatory registration forms through the Registro Unico Empresarial (RUES) portal or the Chamber of Commerce service window; pay the statutory registration fee (based on the subscribed capital) plus the merchant registration fee and register the company in the Registro Mercantil; upon approval, obtain the Chamber's Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation (Certificado de Existencia y Representacion Legal).
required_dossiers: Executed incorporation document (Documento Privado de Constitucion)
Registration application form (Formulario de Registro / RUES)
Copy of the RUT provisional registration of the company (pre-assigned by DIAN if available)
Identification documents of shareholders and legal representative
Name availability certificate
Receipt of payment of registration and merchant fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is suspended pending corrections, respond to the Chamber's electronic or written requirement within the statutory term (generally 10 business days); rectify signatures, attach missing powers of attorney, pay any underpaid registration fee, and request re-examination; a formal appeal can be lodged if the Chamber erroneously denies registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with DIAN: NIT and RUT (Unique Tax Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN - Direccion de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (electronic portal / tax office for the company's address)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Chamber's Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation, file the RUT update via DIAN's MUISCA portal or in-person service; the system assigns the NIT if not previously created; select the tax regime and obligations applicable to an S.A.S. providing services (income tax, complementary taxes, ICA if applicable, and any withholding obligations); obtain the certified RUT.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representacion Legal from the Chamber of Commerce
Certificate of representation and legal representative's identification
Company by-laws / incorporation instrument
Company provisional RUT (if previously assigned)
Email and contact details for digital filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DIAN system rejects the RUT update or the application is queried for incorrect tax classification, correct the declared economic activities (ISIC 7310 / CIUU Rev. 4 code) and resubmit; schedule a DIAN appointment to resolve biometric or digital-certificate problems; file an accuracy declaration for the rejected RUT within the given deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legalization of Mandatory Corporate and Accounting Books
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Initiate the shareholder registry book (Libro de Registro de Accionistas), minutes book (Libro de Actas), and the company's accounting books; request the Chamber of Commerce to legalize (seal/stamp) the books or register the digital certification thereof; this step is required before the books are used for recording share movements and corporate minutes.
required_dossiers: Company incorporation registration certificate
Physical books in an approved commercial format (when applicable)
Company NIT/RUT and certified legal representation documents
Written petition for legalization of corporate books
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber rejects the books for format or folio-number issues, replace or correct the book format under Chamber requirements and resubmit; for digital books, re-upload the authenticated ledger format within the indicated correction period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Commercial and Tax Registration (Registro de Industria y Comercio and Complementary Taxes)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Treasury / Secretaria Distrital de Hacienda (municipal mayor's office of Bogota or the city of the registered office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Registro de Industria y Comercio (ICA) declaration through the municipal tax platform or the local Chamber of Commerce 'ventanilla unica' if offered; specify the company's activity as advertising and public relations services using the ISIC 7310 classification; upon registration, the company must comply with periodic ICA filing and payment of the municipal tax and any complementary taxes; obtain the municipal certificate of activity registration.
required_dossiers: RUT/NIT certificate
Chamber of Commerce Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation
Board resolution confirming the municipal address and activity
Lease contract or property title for the registered office
ICA pre-registration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal authority classifies the activity under a wrong tariff heading, submit a rectification petition attaching the company's purpose clause and a service description to confirm the correct ISIC 7310 classification; respond to objections within the statutory term before the municipality issues a final determination.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Occupational, Civil Defense, and Fire-Safety Clearance for Office Premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Secretaria Distrital de Gobierno - Bomberos / Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos of the local municipality; and collateral occupational health agencies (ARL/SG-SST)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For the office premises, request the fire-safety technical inspection and certificate (Concepto Tecnico de Seguridad Humana / Certificado de Bomberos); submit the floor plan, occupancy details, and proof of incorporation; in parallel, document the occupational health and safety program (Sistema de Gestion de Seguridad y Salud en el Trabajo - SG-SST) required for any workplace, coordinate the registration of employees with the ARL, and ensure fire extinguishers, emergency exits, and first-aid equipment are in place.
required_dossiers: Letter of application for fire-safety certification
Copy of lease or property title for the office
Building/floor plan showing evacuation routes
Company registration certificate and RUT
SG-SST program statement and ARL affiliation proof for employees
Certificate of compliance with occupational risk standards
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire inspection report identifies deficiencies (inadequate extinguishers, blocked exits), install or correct the required safety measures and request a re-inspection; if the occupational clearance is suspended, submit the missing SG-SST documents, correct risk-classification codes, and obtain a new compliance certificate from the competent authority.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No sectoral industrial license applies to a public-relations and communications services firm (ISIC 7310); municipal Regimen de Industria y Comercio registration and general commercial licensing apply as set out above
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Operating authorization is covered by the Chamber of Commerce merchant registration and the municipal Registro de Industria y Comercio; no separate industrial operating permit is required

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) and the regional autonomous environmental corporation (e.g., CAR) for any physical sites; not applicable to office-based service activity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - office-based professional activity; no full EIA or environmental registration is required under Decree 1076 of 2015 for this scope
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office wastewater and domestic discharges must comply with Resolution 0631 of 2015 effluent limits where municipal sewer discharge is used; general solid-waste handling and periodic separation obligations under Resolution 754 of 2022/Decree 1077 of 2015; any vehicles or hardware used (communications servers, electronics) must follow e-waste disposal obligations under Resolution 1512 of 2010 and the applicable hazardous-waste management rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certificate issued by the local Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos for the office premises (fire extinguishers, evacuation plan, unobstructed exits); structural load certificate for the building if required by municipal building codes; mandatory workplace and occupational health clearance pursuant to SG-SST under Decree 1072 of 2015 and Law 1562 of 2012, covering employee risk assessments, ARL enrollment, and training records.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) – official portal: www.dian.gov.co (DIAN Virtual Office/User Authorization Service).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity (including an S.A.S. with non-resident shareholders) must obtain a NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) by registering with DIAN through an appointed attorney-in-fact in Colombia. The procedure requires filing the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) online via DIAN's MUISCA platform, submitting certified corporate documents, proving the legal representative's power, and obtaining a NIT plus RUT certificate before carrying out taxable activities. Foreign entities may also need a local tax residency certificate from their home jurisdiction and, for invoicing purposes, an active electronic invoicing resolution issued by DIAN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombia does not operate a check-the-box regime comparable to the U.S.; the S.A.S. is always taxed at entity level subject to normal corporate income tax (currently 35% for 2025). However, select elections are available under Colombian law: (1) the 'transparencia fiscal' election applicable to certain collective investment vehicle-like structures and special limited vehicles; (2) the option to apply presumed income thresholds and/or special exemption regimes for 'companies classified as newly created and innovative' under Law 1955 of 2019; and (3) anti-hybrid and cross-border tax classification elections may be required where the U.S. or EU check-the-box rules create double-debt or mismatches, to be neutralized under Law 2010 of 2019, Law 2277 of 2022, and the OECD Multilateral Instrument as adopted locally.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Impuesto sobre las Ventas – IVA) supplemented by national consumption taxes and withholding at source; no general sales-and-use tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory IVA registration for persons (including S.A.S. entities) whose gross income from sales of goods or services in the immediately preceding tax year exceeds 3,500 UVT (i.e., approximately COP 169,225,000 for 2025, using UVT of COP 48,350), unless the activity consists solely of exempt or zero-rated exports. Threshold is adjusted annually by DIAN based on the UVT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing (factura electrónica de venta) for all IVA-registered persons. Invoices and equivalent supporting documents must be issued in the XML layout approved by DIAN and transmitted through cloud providers or DIAN's free MUISCA web service. DIAN performs real-time fiscal validation (validación previa) before each invoice receives a digital stamp (CUDE/CUFE status code); large taxpayers must use API/web-service integration. No local clearance is required for export documents, but the electronic export invoice must be matched with the customs declaration SIDUNE and CAN in the same virtual channel.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Sales of tangible goods and services physically exported to third countries (including services rendered to non-resident companies for offshore use, such as international public relations and communication services) are eligible for 0% IVA, provided the exporter is an IVA-registered taxable person, the buyer is abroad, and the service is not considered to be consumed in Colombia. Export eligibility is evidenced by a valid Form 110? / export invoice, the customs export declaration (declaración de exportación), and the service must support a genuine foreign exchange inflow from the overseas principal.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación – DEX) submitted through the Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales' MUISCA or SIGLO XXI system
Bill of Lading (on board ocean or air waybill) naming the Colombian seller as consignor/shipper and the overseas customer as consignee

Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Compensación de Divisas) issued by an authorized Colombian intermediary financial institution, evidencing receipt of proceeds within the required foreign-exchange repatriation window
Commercial invoice with export endorsement and IVA zero-rated item codes
Valid electronic invoice with DIAN digital stamp
Documentation of the contractual service agreement / purchase order
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN audits export transactions through cross-matching customs declarations, electronic invoices, and FX remittances. If zero-rating is found to be fraudulent or the foreign currency not legally repatriated, the entity must pay the omitted IVA (19%) plus interest from the date of sale and a penalty of up to 200% of the total tax evaded; criminal charges can follow under the Colombian anti-counterfeiting/anti-contraband regime (Ley 1762 de 2015). For non-fraudulent but invalid zero-rating claims, statutory interest (12% annual) and a late-payment surcharge of 5% to 10% per month apply, and the exporter may be disqualified from using direct export refund procedures for up to 2 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República (Central Bank of Colombia), acting jointly with the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia and the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit for the administration of Colombia's foreign exchange control regime
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia maintains current-account convertibility. Profits, dividends, interest, royalties and residual capital may be remitted abroad provided the underlying inward investment has been registered with Banco de la República through a Foreign Investment Registration Certificate. Capital-account operations (foreign debt, FDI contributions and portfolio investments) must be channelled through authorized foreign-exchange intermediaries and declared on the corresponding exchange declaration. Colombian residents may keep foreign currency domestically in foreign-denominated accounts or abroad without prior approval, but all income-producing and collection operations relating to goods, services and investments must be validated by the local exchange market framework. For an overseas PR and communications firm whose revenues arise from foreign clients, the main convertibility hurdle is documentary proof of service invoicing and compliance with transfer-pricing rules, rather than an outright convertibility restriction on fee earnings.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Although this business supplies cross-border services rather than physical exports, Colombia's general exchange regime applies to the collection of service receivables in foreign currency. Receivables must be collected within the legal terms established by Banco de la República (as a default, within 4 to 10 months for merchandise exports, with analogous terms for export-of-services operations depending on the contractual milestone). All foreign currency received for Colombian renderings of services must be canalized through an authorized intermediary, meaning the funds must be brought into the formal financial system by means of a local or foreign-currency account and reported on an exchange declaration. There is no universal compulsory surrender requirement, but any conversion into pesos must be executed at the prevailing interbank market rate and recorded as a Colombian peso conversion. Custody arrangements using a foreign bank account (cuenta de compensación) are allowed if declared, and settlement of operational retainer invoices through SWIFT MT103 wires is permissible. The critical compliance threshold is that the services must genuinely be performed in or from Colombia by the S.A.S., otherwise the income may be recharacterized as a mere conduit collection subject to higher withholding or as an impermissible use of the exchange regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_timeline_and_r: Colombian exchange law does not impose a fixed mandatory conversion ratio on export or service proceeds. The statutory requirement is timely repatriation to an authorized banking entity, followed by a voluntary conversion to COP or retention in a permitted foreign-currency account. Administrative practice requires settlement through the exchange market within the applicable term, and failure to comply can trigger fines by the Superintendencia Financiera. For cash-flow planning, a Colombian S.A.S. acting as a global PR agency should establish a Treasury Policy of converting a minimum of 50% of monthly USD retainers to COP to fund domestic payroll and VAT, while keeping the residual 50% in a USD operational account for future disbursements, subject always to eligibility for such holding under local bank account terms.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Investment Escrow and USD Operational Account
Colombian Peso Current Account – Designed for Professional Service Fees
Corporate Transactor with MIC/Caboto clearance capability

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low direct viability combined with legal opportunities. Colombia does not grant direct banking licenses to foreign electronic money institutions, and a Colombian S.A.S. may not open a settlement account with an unregulated offshore EMI as its principal operating account without losing the benefits of the local exchange regime. Foreign EMIs such as Wise, Payoneer or Airwallex may be used for pre-commercial collection of small retainers, but the resulting balances must eventually be repatriated to a Colombian bank, declared under the exchange regime and subject to company tax in Colombia. The higher compliance pathway is to appoint a locally regulated bank as treasury anchor and utilize an EMI only as an invoicing convenience for low-dollar freelance media-sourcing advances; for these purposes, the EMI contract must be fully documented in the corporate treasury policy and reconciled monthly to prevent unfiled foreign accounts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No absolute physical mandate for foreign directors exists under Colombian commercial law. A Colombian S.A.S. may be incorporated remotely because its bylaws may be executed by a non-resident via electronic signature where applicable, but in practice the opening of a corporate bank account will trigger an enhanced due-diligence interview of the legal representative. The recommended protocol is to appoint a Colombian-based administrator or legal counsel with a personal Colombian Tax ID (Cédula de Ciudadanía or NIT) who appears for an in-person or hybrid video interview before the bank's compliance officer. If the foreign director remains the sole legal representative, most tier-1 banks will require an initial physical appearance with the original passport, an apostilled power of attorney, and a certified copy of the certificate of incorporation and bylaws. Remote opening is possible with a local proxy appointed as legal representative for banking purposes, but the bank will still verify all beneficial owners at the 25% threshold.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Non-resident shareholder injecting more than USD 250,000 in capital without audited bank statements or evidence of existing PR operating history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder's last 12 months of domain-bank account statements showing traceable funds; notarized and apostilled declaration of funds' source; audited prior-year financial statements; signed retainer contracts from named overseas clients; CRS/CBC-R notification if the shareholder is subject to automatic exchange of information; Colombian legal entity tax registry (RUT) and certified commercial registration from Cámara de Comercio.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Back-to-back intercompany loans between the S.A.S. and a related foreign PR agency used to fund working capital
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed intercompany loan agreement with arm's-length interest rate and repayment schedule; transfer-pricing file prepared according to Colombian Rules in the form of a 'Informe Estándar País por País' and local Form 120; evidence of real substantive activities (press release production, media relation reports, crisis-communication audits and acquisition of media lists); intra-group service invoices and VAT-neutral analysis under Article 437, 481 and 486 of the Colombian Tax Code.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Unexplained high-frequency receivables from digital advertisement and social-influencer platforms not corroborated by the client registry
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed monthly revenue schedule matching each wire with an itemized retainer invoice; media-buying evidence (Meta Ads, Google Ads, Amazon RMN) showing that the S.A.S. executes campaigns from Colombia; API-level reporting from social platforms to demonstrate that the digital PR service is actually rendered; client verification through chambers-of-commerce certificates or safe-briefing email documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Economic-beneficial-owner entity registered in a high-tax or offshore jurisdiction without economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Beneficial-ownership register from the offshore entity; evidence of tax residency of each beneficial owner in a jurisdiction different from the account; assumed name and apostille certificate; film-and-media distribution rights agreement if relevant; risk explanation memorandum confirming why the offshore holding structure is used for international contracting efficiencies rather than tax evasion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: The bank identifies inconsistent activity when the S.A.S. opens rapidly after its incorporation without meaningful local employees or office
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease agreement for a commercial or virtual office located in Bogotá or Medellín; proof of employment contract for at least one manager and one content specialist resident in Colombia; Colombian social security enrolment (EPS/ARL/FP) showing local substantive presence; quarterly income-tax return drafts; and corporate minutes authorizing the bank relationship.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For equity injections, the S.A.S. must first file the foreign investment registration with Banco de la República via the authorized local bank, identifying the foreign shareholder, the amount and instrument type. The inward remittance is typically settled through SWIFT MT103 with a purpose code 'Foreign Direct Investment – Capital Contributions' (frequently validated by the local bank's system as 'DEInversión extranjera directa – capital'). Upon receiving the USD amount into the USD pre-escrow account, the bank will complete a Colombian foreign-exchange declaration (Declaración de Cambio) and issue the Foreign Investment Certificate. For revenue funds originating from overseas clients, the inbound SWIFT message should carry the purpose code of 'Income from Services' with the relevant payment-circuit name; the firm should monitor that no single payment exceeds the thresholds which trigger mandatory documentation of the investment registration (for non-resident clients no registration is required). All inbound client remittances must be treated as ordinary revenue, only the eventual distribution of profits abroad requires a separate FX declaration for the dividend remittance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: When the Colombian S.A.S. pays subcontractors, freelance media makers, external communications consultants, or media-purchase platforms abroad, the preferred rail is a SWIFT MT103 wire drawn from the USD account, or a COP-to-USD conversion executed at a permitted bank, followed by an outgoing MT103. Although this is a service-business treasury, commercial LC (MT700) remains legally available for any purchase of physical promotional goods, printed branded materials, or exhibition equipment from overseas suppliers; for the regular outsourcing of PR production, the firm normally issues invoice-based direct wires rather than LC. Each outgoing disbursement for services purchased abroad must be accompanied by an invoice, a contract, and exchange declaration where the bank requires it. For payments to tax residents in jurisdictions requiring additional records, the S.A.S. will attach a certificate of non-domiciled contractor from the payee when applicable, and perform any statutory withholding at the transfer-pricing general rate.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable COP/USD forward contracts (forward rate agreements) with a locally authorized bank, executed under ISDA templates and recorded with the central exchange register

Non-deliverable forwards limited to hedging of presumed future cash-flows where delivery of the peso leg is not operational, permitted only through a registered financial intermediary during temporary convertibility windows, subject to monthly position confirmation with Banco de la República
COP/USD cross-currency swaps for the purpose of hedging long-term client retainer commitments or the fair value of an intercompany capital account
FX options (vanilla put/call) traded OTC with authorized Colombian banks or through a locally registered brokerage, subject to the general regulation on derivative operations for corporates
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps for external borrowings, only when the S.A.S. takes intercompany or third-party debt, with full transfer-pricing and documentation requirements
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.weekly_liquidity_clearing_protocol: The treasury calendar should be fixed as follows: (i) any USD remittances received between Monday and Thursday are consolidated and converted to COP on Friday morning unless a hedge is active; (ii) no fewer than 20% of total operating funds are kept in USD to settle global media invoices quickly; (iii) the bank is instructed to sweep excess EUR or USD balances above a threshold of USD 40,000 into a term deposit or short-term Colombian TES fund with a repurchase clause; (iv) an MT199 message is not sufficient; all settlement confirms must be MT103/MT202 with the corresponding FX deal number to ensure the local Central Bank exchange declaration is correct.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renewal of the merchant registration (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio (local Chamber of Commerce) via RUES
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 to March 31 of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers coercive fines (multas) set by the Chamber; failure to renew for three consecutive years subjects the company to administrative cancellation from the commercial registry (strike-off).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and management report (Estados Financieros and Informe de Gestión) deposited in the registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio (Chamber of Commerce) and made available to Superintendencia de Sociedades
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements to shareholders by March 31; approval at the annual shareholders' meeting by April 30; deposit with the Chamber within 15 business days after approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or late filing gives rise to fines by the Chamber of Commerce and Superintendencia de Sociedades; persistent failure may lead to formal intervention or administrative cancellation of the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual final beneficial owner (UBO) confirmation report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio through RUES (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually according to the RUES calendar (typically between April and May); in case of any shareholding change, within 30 calendar days of the transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or update UBO information may result in economic sanctions and fines under Colombian anti-money laundering rules, as well as suspension of certificate issuance by the Chamber; repeated non-compliance can trigger a non-operating status and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Minutes of the annual ordinary shareholders' meeting entered in the corporate minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate minute book (inspectable by Cámara de Comercio, DIAN, and Superintendencia de Sociedades)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Meeting must be held no later than one month after the financial statement presentation deadline, i.e., by April 30 of each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold and record the annual meeting does not dissolve the S.A.S., but it exposes directors and officers to regulatory fines, evidentiary obstacles for distributions, and potential judicial intervention.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory auditor's report (Dictamen del Revisor Fiscal), if the company is compulsorily audited
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting and deposit with Cámara de Comercio
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Issued with the financial statements and approved by April 30; deposited with the Chamber within 15 business days after the shareholders' meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omission of the revisor fiscal where legally required subjects the company and its directors to fines from the Superintendencia de Sociedades and may invalidate the financial statement filing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: In Colombia, a Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada (S.A.S.) must appoint a statutory auditor (revisor fiscal) when: (i) gross revenues or total assets at prior year-end equal or exceed 5,000 legal monthly minimum wages (SMMLV); (ii) it qualifies as a public-interest entity or is subject to permanent inspection/surveillance by the Superintendencia de Sociedades; or (iii) the bylaws or shareholders' meeting require one. A low-risk overseas PR communications S.A.S. below these thresholds is not legally required to have a compulsory independent audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Colombian accounting standards based on IFRS (NIIF) as adopted via Decree 2420 of 2015; large entities use Full IFRS and small/medium entities use IFRS for SMEs. Financial statements are expressed in Colombian pesos (COP).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The S.A.S. must maintain an up-to-date share register and, annually, confirm its final beneficial owners through the RUES online portal of the local Chamber of Commerce. The confirmation is made under the annual UBO schedule; any transfer of shares or change in ultimate beneficial ownership must be reported within 30 calendar days. The report must identify each natural-person shareholder or ultimate owner and its national tax identification number.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 - 7,000 for a certified audit (when voluntarily or compulsorily required)
